sources.prompt: READ-ONLY literature slice for goal:g14.3 chain (d), the looped / recurrent-depth transformer line, CPU-first (a 4-core aarch64 box, 23 GB RAM, no GPU). Survey depth-recurrent and looped small language models WITH RELEASED WEIGHTS: Huginn-0125 (Geiping et al. 2025, recurrent depth, 3.5B), Ouro looped LMs (2025, 1.4B / 2.6B), Mixture-of-Recursions (2025), Universal Transformer / ALBERT-style weight tying, Looped Transformers (Giannou 2023; Yang 2024 reasoning), test-time latent reasoning by recurrence, and the owner paper Recurrent Looped Transformer (alphaxiv 2609.recurrent-looped-transformer, TEMPORAL recurrence -- state its difference from depth recurrence explicitly). For EACH: arXiv id, mechanism in two lines, unique params vs effective depth (loops), released weights (HF id, bytes, licence; MEASURED from the HF API today), CPU runnability (transformers or llama.cpp support; any GGUF), one quality number against a non-looped model of the same unique params at the same quality proxy, the training recipe cost if stated. Then a RANKED table for the town: which released looped model can a kid-tier eval run on CPU today (tok/s estimate = bandwidth / bytes x loops), and one falsifiable hypothesis per top-3 row: what would prove looping beats a same-size non-looped model on the town 20-prompt kid checklist. Write README-ranked-table.md + one digest per paper (<= 100 lines each) into the scratch dir; MEASURED vs ESTIMATE tags on every number; no repo modified; anonymization: never name hosts, IPs, providers, GPU models beyond generic classes.

angles.text: DEPTH recurrence iterates a weight-tied block at one position (Huginn/Ouro/MoR/UT) with a runtime loop dial; TEMPORAL recurrence (RLT 2609.recurrent-looped-transformer) carries decoder hidden state + SWA cache across token positions, so effective path = tokens x decoder depth and prompt processing stays sequential. Any town hypothesis must name which.

Looping multiplies CPU memory traffic by the loop count: effective bytes-touched/token = weight_bytes x loops, because 4-core caches cannot hold the model. tok/s ~ BW/(weight_bytes x loops). Measured memcpy on the box 2026-09-18: 23.8 GB/s combined read+write; Ouro-1.4B Q4_K_M (0.896 GB) 13-27 tok/s @1 loop, 3.3-6.7 @4 loops.

Only Ouro has a released looped LM with a working CPU path today (GGUF via a PATCHED llama.cpp; ouro arch not upstream). Huginn has released Apache-2.0 weights but F32 15.63 GB and no GGUF/llama.cpp arch. MoR and Loop-Think-Generalize checkpoints are on external drives. RLT has no weights and no results.
